Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of replication projects, authors of original studies tend to have higher citation metrics compared to authors of replication studies. This hypothesis is based on the comparison of `author_citations_avg.o` (average citations of original study authors) and `author_citations_avg.r` (average citations of replication study authors), as well as `author_citations_max.o` (maximum citations of original study authors) and `author_citations_max.r` (maximum citations of replication study authors). The statistical analysis using independent t-tests revealed significant differences, with p-values of 3.14e-96 and 2.80e-96 for average and maximum citations, respectively, indicating that original study authors have significantly higher citation metrics than replication study authors.
